content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised painterly 3D illustration with the graphic language of a hand-painted game world - bold silhouettes, simplified sculpted forms, soft painterly surfaces without fine photoreal texture detail, and light modelled in clear shapes rather than flat even illumination. Never photorealistic and never live-action, but equally never comic or cartoon. Deep violet and midnight-blue base, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange only for lamplight, backlight and rim light - never as a colour of the network itself. This violet-and-orange palette is present in every frame; the image never desaturates into grey or neutral blue. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. No text, letters, logos, icons or symbols of any kind ever appear anywhere. The dragonfly comes to a stop in the middle of the warm lit office and hovers in place, wings beating hard and fast in powerful soft-blurred strokes, her luminous violet trail continuous and always visible behind her. The people around her are in constant natural motion the whole time: hands typing and sliding across keyboards, a head turning to look up, someone gesturing with both hands while speaking, another nodding in reply, one person walking slowly between the desks, a chair turning. They are simplified graphic figures, sculpted in broad flat shapes and rim light, with no fine clothing detail, no hair detail and no facial features at all, and the room keeps exactly the same painterly language as the rest of the film, never realistic office stock footage. The office is one single long deep open-plan room and stays exactly the same room for the entire shot, never changing its shape, length or proportions. While she hovers, the camera moves in very close to her and travels smoothly all the way around her in one continuous full three hundred and sixty degree orbit, staying close the whole way with the dragonfly large in frame and held sharply in focus, passing her side, her front and her other side before coming back in behind her. Throughout this orbit the office behind her is thrown far out of focus into a soft wash of warm bokeh and glowing highlights: the background is never sharp and never readable while the camera turns, only soft blurred light and colour. As the orbit ends and the camera settles in behind her again, the room comes back into focus. As the orbit completes, the violet network floods out from her through the whole office at once: light lines race along every desk edge and table top, run across the floor, climb the walls and spread over the ceiling, with bright glowing nodes at the junctions, until the entire room from end to end is threaded with violet light. The light stays on the surfaces of the room - along desks, floor, walls and ceiling - and does not hang as a free-floating lattice in mid air. Light lines also reach the people, growing from one person to the next with a calm glowing node beside each of them, until everyone in the room is linked. The network is violet and white only; no orange lines are ever part of it. Everything that lights up stays permanently lit and never fades, dims or goes dark again. Nothing is built or added: the room, the desks and the people were already there, and only the light is new. The camera follows the dragonfly, which leads the shot and stays visible throughout. The camera never pulls back and never loses the dragonfly. The shot ends with the dragonfly clearly in frame ahead of the camera, seen from behind, hovering steadily, her violet trail streaming behind her, the whole room around her filled with glowing violet network.
